teaser.en: A Digo mushroom with a name but, so far, no scientific identity.

summary.en: Chibazi is a mushroom known to Digo collectors that has not yet been scientifically identified. Pakia records little beyond its name.

about.en: *Chibazi* is a mushroom that Digo collectors know by name but that has not yet been scientifically identified. Pakia notes that some of the mushrooms he collected were still awaiting identification when his study was written. Digo collectors tell mushrooms apart mainly by the colour of the cap, but no description of *chibazi* is recorded.

where.en: Digo mushroom collectors recognise three mushroom grounds: *Brachystegia* woodland (*mirihini*), farmland (*mdani*) and termite mounds (*tsuluni*). Which of these this mushroom favours is not recorded.

uses.en: Pakia notes that the Digo give names only to mushrooms they know as edible, so *chibazi* is very likely one that local people collect and eat. Wild mushrooms should only be eaten when identified by someone with expert local knowledge.

culture.en: Mushroom collecting is women's work among the Digo. Pakia found that only about ten kinds, those learnt from the elders as edible, are eaten, and that collectors pick them young, with the cap still closed (*fundula*), because open caps (*bumula*) are usually full of worms.

names.en: Pakia records *chibazi*; the meaning is not explained. Pakia also lists a mushroom called *N'chibalazi*, which may or may not be the same.
